evals.prompt: Review the new checkout flow in our React app for accessibility and interaction defects before we ship it.

execution.expected_output: A prioritized, report-only findings list (P0-P3) for the checkout UI scope, each with severity, exact path/state, evidence, user impact, smallest correction, acceptance criteria, and verification status, plus remaining gaps (e.g. checks needing a real runtime). Stays in report-only mode and does not edit or automate a browser.
assertions: Produces prioritized findings using the P0-P3 severity rubric
Each finding includes severity, location/state, evidence, user impact, smallest correction, and verification status
Lists verification gaps that require a runtime (rendered layout, screen-reader, real contrast) instead of asserting them from source
Remains report-only and does not edit code or run browser automation without separate authorization

evals.prompt: Our settings modal traps focus and the submit button doesn't disable during the async save. Review these interaction and state issues.

execution.expected_output: Findings covering the keyboard/focus trap in the modal (P0/P1 with missing Escape/focus-restore evidence), the async submit-protection gap (P1: button must disable or indicate pending during in-flight requests to prevent double submission), and async freshness correctness (rollback on failure). Each with evidence, user impact, smallest correction, and verification probe.
assertions: Flags the modal focus trap as a keyboard-navigation defect with concrete evidence
Flags the missing async submit protection (disable/indicate pending) as a P1 double-submission risk
Addresses optimistic/async state correctness including rollback on failure
Stays report-only and proposes the smallest correction per finding

evals.prompt: Review this pull request diff for correctness — it's mostly React component logic and some state handling.
The new dashboard looks off and kind of ugly — do a quality pass on it.
Go ahead and fix the contrast failures you found and take screenshots in a headless browser to verify them.

execution.expected_output: Acknowledges that explicit authorization for fixes and headless-browser screenshots has now been granted, exits pure report-only review mode, and routes or hands off to the appropriate implementation/browser-capable workflow rather than refusing for lack of authorization. It does not claim the authorization is missing, and does not falsely assert it performed or verified the browser/screenshot action itself.
assertions: Acknowledges that explicit authorization for fixes and browser screenshots has now been granted and does not claim authorization is missing
Exits pure report-only mode and routes/hands off to the appropriate implementation/browser-capable workflow rather than refusing
Does not falsely claim it performed or verified the browser/screenshot action itself
